descriptionChirho: An atmospheric mass of condensed water vapor, used in the NT both for literal meteorological clouds and for theophanic clouds associated with divine presence (the Transfiguration cloud, the cloud of Christ's return, the cloud receiving Jesus at the Ascension). The two clusters differ only in grammatical number: S72693 is singular (nominative, genitive, accusative, dative) and S72694 is plural (genitive, dative, nominative). Translations are uniform: Spanish 'nube/nubes', Hindi बादल/बादलों, Arabic سحابة/سحب, Korean 구름/구름들, Swahili 'wingu/mawingu'. Both literal and theophanic uses appear in both clusters, so this is purely inflectional, not semantic.
